description: Magazine page type vocabulary. Every rule references a feature produced by babeldoc/magazine/page_features.py, compares it with one of ge/le/gt/lt against a threshold, and contributes its weight when satisfied. A positive weight is evidence for the type; a negative weight is a penalty that withdraws evidence when the page shows something the type rules out. A type scores its satisfied weight, positive and negative summed, over its positive weight alone, clamped to 0..1, so a type that trips no penalty can still reach 1.0. Weights may not be zero, and every type needs some positive weight and at least one positive weight ge/gt rule, because only a rule of that shape is satisfied by a quantity the page actually carries. With require_positive_evidence set, a type scores 0 on a page satisfying none of its positive weight ge/gt rules, so a page carrying nothing cannot sweep the le/lt rules of a type it shows no sign of being. Thresholds and weights are tuning parameters: retune them here from the report produced by tools/page_classify_report.py, never in code. Two optional policy flags concern articles and they are not interchangeable. starts_article is the chain detector's prior, meaning running text does not continue into this page; it is declared on every type that is not flowing body text, furniture included, because no article runs into a bought page either. opens_article means an article begins on this page, which furniture does not do: a contents page is somewhere text begins without being somewhere an article begins, and declaring it as one made it absorb the feature page after it. Both default to false when a type declares neither. A third optional flag, preserve_line_structure, is about layout rather than articles: it says the page sets records one to a line, so a paragraph the finder assembled out of several source lines is not a translation unit and is cut back into them. It is declared on the two types whose lines are records rather than prose and defaults to false everywhere else. A fourth optional flag, indent_eligible, is layout as well and narrower still: it says the page sets running body text whose first line a paragraph convention may be written for, and it is declared on the two types that carry an article's prose. It is not declared anywhere else, and defaults to false, because a convention written for prose is wrong for a page of records, for a credit list and for a field of captions; a page whose kind nobody has thought about is more likely to be one of those than to be an article, and leaving such a page as the source set it is the answer that cannot be wrong twice.

page_types.name: front_cover
page_types.description: Opening publication cover: issue masthead or publication identity with dominant artwork and little running text; a standalone product promotion is an advertisement instead.

page_types.name: back_cover
page_types.description: Closing cover: last page of the issue, image led, very little text.

page_types.name: toc
page_types.description: Navigational contents index: several entry or section titles repeatedly paired with page numbers in rows, columns or a grid; it may occupy only one region of a composite page.

page_types.name: masthead
page_types.description: Publication imprint and credits: staff lists, publisher, addresses, ISSN, copyright or legal lines, usually set small; not a signed editor's letter.

page_types.name: editorial
page_types.description: Editor's letter or signed foreword: one continuous personal argument, commonly with a portrait, signature or editor attribution; not general front-of-book prose.

page_types.name: article_opener
page_types.description: First page of a named story: headline markedly larger than body text, commonly a deck, byline or author block, followed by the beginning of prose; artwork is optional.

page_types.name: article_body
page_types.description: Continuation of one story: substantial running prose at body size, commonly in columns; subheads, pull quotes, drop caps, pictures or charts may appear without changing its role.

page_types.name: photo_spread
page_types.description: Editorial photograph or illustration dominates the page while running prose is absent or minor; it may carry a display phrase, quotation or caption and need not be full bleed.

page_types.name: infographic
page_types.description: Explanatory data or process page whose central communication is a chart, map, diagram, timeline or labelled graphic rather than an ordinary photograph.

page_types.name: interview
page_types.description: Question and answer page: alternating short prompts and longer replies in two type sizes.

page_types.name: sidebar_heavy
page_types.description: Page visibly divided into several independent modules, briefs, boxes or side stories; ordinary columns and varied type within one continuous article are not sufficient.

page_types.name: contributors
page_types.description: Collection of several short author or contributor biographies, often with one portrait per person; bylines or quoted experts inside one continuing story do not qualify.

page_types.name: letters_page
page_types.description: Reader correspondence: several medium length signed items with no artwork.

page_types.name: advertisement
page_types.description: Commercial promotion: product or service focus, prominent brand or logo, slogan, offer, QR code or call to action, usually with little editorial running text.

page_types.name: section_divider
page_types.description: Sparse thematic section break: a section title or theme with little prose and without the headline, byline, deck and body apparatus of a named article.
